summary.en: U.S. Defence Secretary Hegseth traveled to Caracas and signed a new military partnership agreement with the interim Venezuelan government, expanding cooperation to target drug trafficking and positioning Venezuela as a compliant security partner. The deal was sealed during meetings with interim president and Delcy Rodriguez, while Colombia rejected a joint U.S. plan to target drug gangs, indicating regional tension over security initiatives. The United States also announced a Caribbean operation, during which a marine died after falling overboard. Two battle-related deaths occurred in 2007, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: U.S. forsvarsminister Hegseth reiste til Caracas og signerte en ny militær partnerskapsavtale med den midlertidige venezuelanske regjeringen, som utvider samarbeidet for å bekjempe narkotikahandel og gjør Venezuela til en etterfølgende sikkerhetspartner. Avtalen ble inngått under møter med den midlertidige presidenten og Delcy Rodriguez, mens Colombia avviste en felles amerikansk plan for å gå mot narkotikagjenger, noe som viser regional spenning rundt sikkerhetsinitiativer. USA kunngjorde også en karibisk operasjon, der en marine døde etter å ha falt overbord. To dødsfall i kamp ble registrert i 2007, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Crisis in Venezuela
background.extract: An ongoing socioeconomic and political crisis began in Venezuela during the presidencies of Hugo Chávez, Nicolás Maduro as well as Delcy Rodríguez. It has been marked by hyperinflation, starvation, disease, crime, and mortality rates, resulting in massive emigration. Food shortages and hyperinflation have ended, but inflation remains high. It is the worst economic crisis in Venezuela's history and considered by some sources as more severe than the Great Depression in the United States, the 1985–1994 Brazilian economic crisis, or the 2008–2009 hyperinflation in Zimbabwe. In 2019, the Institute of International Finance called it the single largest economic collapse outside of war in 45 years. Writers have compared aspects, such as unemployment and GDP contraction, to Bosnia and Herzegovina after the 1992–95 Bosnian War, and those in Russia, Cuba and Albania following the Revolutions of 1989.
